note: The plan. Every unit of every sentence track belongs to exactly one stage, in the order to learn them. A unit only opens when the unit before it in its own track is mostly met (and a track may wait for a unit of another track), so keep each track's units in order. Add a unit: put "pack.unit" in the stage where it belongs. tools/validate.mjs checks that no unit is missing or listed twice and that the order respects the unlock rules.

stages.title: First steps
stages.blurb: Where things are, big and small, and the first greetings.

stages.title: I want, I do
stages.blurb: Say what you want and what you do, and talk yourself through a morning.

stages.title: Yesterday and tomorrow
stages.blurb: The past and the future of everyday verbs, and retelling your day.

stages.title: People and places
stages.blurb: Family and friends, going to and from places, and your first real conversations.

stages.title: Who does what to whom
stages.blurb: Subjects and objects, questions, and changing a sentence for I, you, we and they.

stages.title: Past and future, automatic
stages.blurb: More past and future, one or many, saying “not”, and a conversation at home.

stages.title: Numbers, time and orders
stages.blurb: Counting, telling the hour, giving and taking orders, saying what you like.

stages.title: Roman life
stages.blurb: Meals, hospitality, famous sayings, small talk, habits, and how Romans shouted and swore.

stages.title: Belonging and giving
stages.blurb: Whose is it, giving and telling, and more verbs.

stages.title: The genitive in depth
stages.blurb: Of the whole, of quality and value, with adjectives, and with “remember”.

stages.title: More declensions, more pronouns
stages.blurb: The fourth and fifth declensions, and I, you and we in every case.

stages.title: Latin on the wall
stages.blurb: Pompeii graffiti, tombstones and famous lines from the authors.

stages.title: This, that, who
stages.blurb: Point at things, say him and her, and join sentences with who and which.

stages.title: Himself, better, by means
stages.blurb: Point back at the subject, compare things, and use the ablative for with, by and because of.

stages.title: The Roman world
stages.blurb: Law, war, home, gods, nature, thought, travel and time, in words that Latin authors use again and again.
